abstract: Large, well-annotated datasets are essential for developing medical artificial intelligence models, yet data sharing is often restricted by privacy regulations. Synthetic images may help address this limitation if they preserve diagnostic information while reducing the risk of reproducing patient data. We developed a diffusion autoencoder-based framework for class-conditional synthetic chest CT generation that incorporates latent-space distance filtering to reduce the likelihood of regenerating training samples. A diffusion autoencoder was trained on the public RSNA 2020 Pulmonary Embolism (PE) dataset. PE-positive and PE-negative images were synthesized by sampling latent representations from class-specific kernel density estimates. Samples with a nearest-neighbor latent-space distance below a predefined threshold were rejected. To assess diagnostic utility, ResNet-50 classifiers were trained across 10 independent runs using real, synthetic, or mixed real-synthetic datasets. Performance was evaluated on a held-out real test set using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), with DeLong 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Models trained on synthetic data achieved an AUC of 0.862 (95% CI, 0.851-0.874), only slightly lower than models trained on real data (AUC = 0.872, 95% CI, 0.861-0.883) and mixed real-synthetic data (AUC = 0.865, 95% CI, 0.855-0.876). These differences were statistically significant (p < 0.05) but small in absolute terms. A nearest-neighbor copy-detection analysis of 38,000 synthetic slices found no direct copies of real training images. These findings indicate that the synthetic CT images preserve diagnostically meaningful information for image-level PE classification while incorporating measures intended to enhance privacy awareness and reduce similarity to real patient data.
zh_abstract: 大规模、标注良好的数据集对于开发医学人工智能模型至关重要，但数据共享常常受到隐私法规的限制。如果合成图像能够保留诊断信息，同时降低复现患者数据的风险，则可能有助于解决这一限制。我们开发了一种基于扩散自编码器的类别条件合成胸部CT生成框架，该框架引入潜空间距离过滤，以降低重新生成训练样本的可能性。扩散自编码器在公开的RSNA 2020肺栓塞（PE）数据集上训练。通过从类别特异性核密度估计中采样潜在表征，合成PE阳性和PE阴性图像。最近邻潜空间距离低于预设阈值的样本被剔除。为评估诊断效用，我们使用真实、合成或真实-合成混合数据集，进行了10次独立运行的ResNet-50分类器训练。在留出的真实测试集上，采用受试者工作特征曲线下面积（AUC）及DeLong 95%置信区间（CI）评估性能。在合成数据上训练的模型AUC为0.862（95% CI，0.851-0.874），仅略低于在真实数据上训练的模型（AUC = 0.872，95% CI，0.861-0.883）和在真实-合成混合数据上训练的模型（AUC = 0.865，95% CI，0.855-0.876）。这些差异具有统计学意义（p < 0.05），但绝对差值很小。对38,000张合成切片进行的最近邻复制检测分析未发现真实训练图像的直接复制。这些结果表明，合成CT图像保留了对图像层面PE分类具有诊断意义的信息，同时纳入了旨在增强隐私意识并降低与真实患者数据相似度的措施。

abstract: Patients with Multiple Long-Term Conditions (MLTCs), also known as multimorbidity, often present clinical and operational challenges in emergency departments (EDs), yet how their care pathways deviate from expected workflows remains underexplored. This study introduces a process-aware analytical framework that quantifies and interprets ED process deviations by integrating multi-perspective conformance checking with explainable machine learning. Using routinely collected Scottish ED data between 2017-2023, we derived an empirical benchmark pathway. We introduced a new metric, the deviation score (DS), which captures both structural misalignments and breaches of the four-hour ED standard, a national service target defined as completion of ED care within four hours of arrival. Compared with non-MLTC attendances, MLTC patients exhibited longer and more complex pathways, higher DS values, and lower conformance to the benchmark model. The framework enabled interpretable SHAP analyses, revealing that deviation severity among MLTC attendances was primarily associated with triage acuity, year of attendance, activity queue length (number of patients queuing for the same care activity), and referral source, with additional contributions from age, arrival time, and number of chronic conditions. Threshold effects were observed in both queue length and multimorbidity burden, beyond which deviation severity increased sharply, suggesting points where standard pathways become harder to maintain. These findings show that deviation severity for MLTC patients is shaped by clinical urgency and system-level pressures at presentation. However, the inherent complexity of MLTC patients may further increase vulnerability to deviation. The framework offers the potential foundation for process evaluation and targeted improvement in emergency care.

title: SYNDRI: Context-aware removal of transcript spillover in imaging-based spatial transcriptomics

abstract: Imaging-based spatial transcriptomics (ST) measures gene expression at single-cell resolution, but imperfect segmentation often misassigns transcripts between neighboring cells, a problem known as transcript spillover. This spillover is niche-dependent and can therefore confound downstream analyses that rely on niche-specific differential expression. True spillover cannot be directly quantified in experimental ST data, so existing correction methods infer contamination indirectly from transcript positions or expression structure. Here we introduce SYNDRI, a post-segmentation correction method that frames spillover detection as a supervised, gene-level classification task. We develop SYNDRI-SIM to generate labeled training data by simulating spillover between spatially mapped scRNA-seq profiles. SYNDRI uses a transformer to predict gene-level spillover probabilities conditioned on each cell's expression, identity, and local neighborhood, without requiring transcript-level coordinates or deconvolution. On held-out simulated data, SYNDRI achieves an AUPRC of 0.86, compared with 0.64 for the next-best method. Across MERFISH, CosMx, and Xenium datasets, SYNDRI achieves the highest aggregate performance across metrics of cell-type separation, reference similarity, and preservation of within-cell-type heterogeneity. In a CosMx lung cancer dataset, SYNDRI removes nearly all potentially contaminating tumor and macrophage markers from differential expression between tumor-associated and stromal fibroblasts while retaining native fibroblast markers. These results demonstrate the utility of learning from simulated spillover to improve the interpretation of spatial gene expression.
zh_abstract: 基于成像的空间转录组学（ST）可在单细胞分辨率下测量基因表达，但不完善的分割常导致转录本在相邻细胞间被错误归属，这一问题称为转录本溢出（transcript spillover）。这种溢出依赖于微环境（niche），因此可能混淆依赖微环境特异性差异表达的下游分析。真实的溢出无法在实验性ST数据中直接量化，因此现有校正方法通过转录本位置或表达结构间接推断污染。在此我们提出SYNDRI，一种分割后校正方法，将溢出检测视为有监督的基因水平分类任务。我们开发了SYNDRI-SIM，通过在空间映射的scRNA-seq谱之间模拟溢出来生成带标签的训练数据。SYNDRI使用Transformer，根据每个细胞的表达、身份及局部邻域预测基因水平的溢出概率，无需转录本水平坐标或反卷积。在留出的模拟数据上，SYNDRI的AUPRC为0.86，而次优方法为0.64。在MERFISH、CosMx和Xenium数据集中，SYNDRI在细胞类型分离、参考相似性以及保留细胞类型内部异质性等指标上取得了最高的综合表现。在CosMx肺癌数据集中，SYNDRI在肿瘤相关成纤维细胞与基质成纤维细胞的差异表达中去除了几乎所有可能的污染性肿瘤和巨噬细胞标志物，同时保留了成纤维细胞固有标志物。这些结果证明了从模拟溢出中学习对改善空间基因表达解读的价值。

abstract: [Dentistry journal] Objective: Tumor-associated calcification is increasingly recognized as a potentially relevant feature of the tumor microenvironment across multiple malignancies; however, its significance in oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) remains poorly understood and is frequently overlooked during routine histopathologic assessment. This perspective examines the potential of artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted computational pathology to improve the detection, quantification, and spatial characterization of tumor-associated calcification in OSCC and discusses its potential as an emerging histopathologic research phenotype and candidate biomarker requiring further validation. Design: A narrative synthesis of the current literature was undertaken to evaluate the biological mechanisms underlying tumor-associated calcification in OSCC, recent advances in biomineralization research, and the application of AI and computational pathology in digital histopathology. Results: Current evidence indicates that calcification has been reported or proposed in vascular, stromal, necrotic, and extracellular matrix-associated contexts in OSCC and related pathological settings; however, the prevalence, biological mechanisms, and reproducibility of these patterns in OSCC remain insufficiently characterized. Advances in whole-slide imaging, deep learning, and computational pathology have enabled automated tissue segmentation, feature extraction, and quantitative histopathologic analysis. However, their application to the systematic detection and spatial characterization of calcification in OSCC remains limited. abstract: [Journal of functional morphology and kinesiology] Background: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly applied to physiological prediction, physical activity monitoring, and personalized exercise prescription. However, evidence regarding its practical effectiveness remains heterogeneous. This systematic review examined applications of AI, machine learning (ML), and deep learning (DL) in exercise-related prediction, monitoring, and personalization among adults. Methods: Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, PubMed and Scopus were searched for studies published between 2015 and 2025, with Google Scholar used as a supplementary source. Eligibility followed PICO: adults aged 18 years or older (P); AI, ML, or DL applications for exercise prediction, monitoring, or personalization (I); conventional or non-personalized approaches, where applicable (C); and predictive accuracy and physiological, functional, or behavioral exercise outcomes (O). Findings were synthesized descriptively. Results: Ten studies were included: four examined physiological or energy-expenditure prediction, two investigated activity-related behavioral outcomes, two evaluated training-response classification or recommendation generation, and two assessed AI-personalized exercise interventions. Predictive models demonstrated promising performance in specific applications, although validation procedures and populations varied substantially. The intervention studies reported greater perceived exercise intensity and satisfaction in one trial and improvements in selected measures of balance, flexibility, and strength in another. Conclusions: AI-based approaches show potential for supporting exercise assessment, monitoring, and individualized decision-making. However, evidence regarding their superiority over conventional exercise prescription remains limited by the small number of intervention studies, methodological heterogeneity, and insufficient external validation. Further well-designed, long-term intervention studies are needed to establish their comparative effectiveness and practical benefits.

abstract: [Journal of fungi (Basel, Switzerland)] The need for precise classification of fungi from microscopic images plays a critical role in diagnosing and treating patients since it requires timeliness and effectiveness. Therefore, this work proposes a new approach to explainable deep learning for fungal image classification and report generation. The developed framework consists of four pre-trained convolutional neural network models-DenseNet121, ResNet18, VGG16, and InceptionV3-which are used to classify fungal microscopic images into five classes. abstract: Accurate and early classification of brain tumours from magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is essential for treatment planning, yet many published deep learning studies are trained and tested on small, single-source datasets, reporting accuracies that may not hold outside these datasets. This study compares six deep learning architectures for four-class classification (healthy, meningioma, glioma and pituitary tumour): a baseline convolutional neural network (CNN), an attention-based CNN, ShuffleNet, and EfficientNet-B0, ResNet-50 and Xception augmented with the Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM). The models were trained on a corpus assembled from four publicly available MRI datasets. Because these datasets carry no patient identifiers, a leakage-aware pipeline was developed that removes exact duplicates using MD5 hashing (550 images) and near-duplicates using perceptual hashing (8,024 images), and assigns visually similar images to the same fold during 5-fold group cross-validation. A leave-one-dataset-out (LODO) test on a fully held-out dataset was used to measure cross-dataset generalisation. Under a conventional random split, ShuffleNet achieved 97.1% accuracy with 1.2M parameters. Under leakage-aware group K-fold cross-validation, ShuffleNetV2 (98.41%) and EfficientNet-B0 (98.23%) were statistically indistinguishable (paired t-test, p = 0.19), and both significantly outperformed the custom CNNs. On the held-out dataset, accuracy dropped for every model: EfficientNet-B0 generalised best (78.4%), while ShuffleNetV2 fell to 66.2%. Glioma-meningioma confusion was the dominant error mode, and Grad-CAM maps showed that predictions were driven by tumour regions. These results indicate that in-distribution accuracy alone overstates real-world performance and that leakage-aware and cross-dataset evaluation should be reported alongside it.

abstract: Path-traced rendering shows CT and MR volumes with realistic lighting, but it restarts after every change of view, clipping plane or transfer function (TF), the map from voxel intensity to colour and opacity, which limits the frame rate. Feed-forward Gaussian splatting models such as RenderFM predict the Gaussians directly from the volume instead of fitting them to each scan, and are fast. RenderFM, however, handles only CT, runs its network again after every TF edit, has no clipping operator, and places its Gaussians on a uniform 3-mm grid that blurs organ boundaries and cut faces. We present RenderFM-Next, a feed-forward model that addresses these limits. One network handles both CT and MR. Its Gaussians are predicted once per volume: a new TF needs no pass of this network, and a clipping plane cuts them exactly, using operators from prior work. The model predicts coarse 3-mm Gaussians for the whole volume and refines them to 1.5 mm only where refinement improves the image. A small score head ranks the coarse Gaussians by how much refining them would reduce the rendering error; at render time the user chooses how many are refined, and those next to a clipping plane are always refined, which sharpens cut faces. We build a benchmark of about 2,000 CT and MR scans with path-traced references under clinical presets, TF edits and clipping. Our RenderFM-Next improves over RenderFM retrained on this benchmark by 2.8 dB on CT and 2.4 dB on MR and renders a 1600x1600 view in 4-6 ms. Refinement adds 0.30 / 0.69 dB over the same model trained without it (0.51 / 1.17 dB on cut faces), and refining a learned 10% of the coarse Gaussians matches a random 50% with 2.4x fewer Gaussians. abstract: Clinical tests, such as the oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT), perturb a physiological system at rest and record its excursion over a fixed protocol window as a short, undersampled time series. Such curves rarely allow parameter identification at the individual level, yet their trends carry physiological information that emerges at the population level as recurrent response patterns. Standard clustering methods aggregate differences globally and average out those trends, losing precisely the information about how the system regains control after the perturbation; identifying response patterns requires a method that preserves them. We present a nonparametric framework that factorizes each curve into unit waveforms, sorts them with a symbolic trend-compatibility filter, and compares compatible shapes using discrete Sobolev-type distances on finite differences up to order $k$. The number of clusters, i.e., distinct response types, equals the number of realizable trend patterns the cohort populates, validated by resampling. Applied to 1283 five-point OGTTs, the method identifies 7 glycemia and 8 insulinemia types. The count holds across a threefold range of resolution. In benchmarks against six classical clustering methods, ours alone never mixes opposite trends, with comparable reconstruction error and stability. Clinical normality, assessed after clustering, is graded, overlapping, and distributed unevenly across response types ($h=0.14$--$0.48$). Overall, our method distinguishes response types among curves too short for alignment-based methods yet too informative for reduction to summary values. It applies to any protocol recording a system's response to a standardized perturbation on a short grid.
zh_abstract: 口服葡萄糖耐量试验（OGTT）等临床检查会对处于静息状态的生理系统施加扰动，并在固定的方案窗口内将其偏移记录为一条短而欠采样的时间序列。此类曲线很少能在个体水平上进行参数识别，但其趋势所携带的生理信息会在人群水平上表现为反复出现的反应模式。标准聚类方法在全局层面汇总差异，从而将这些趋势平均掉，恰恰丢失了系统在扰动后如何恢复控制的信息；识别反应模式需要一种能够保留这些趋势的方法。我们提出一种非参数框架：将每条曲线分解为单位波形，用符号化的趋势相容性过滤器对其分类，并在相容的形状之间使用基于不超过 $k$ 阶有限差分的离散 Sobolev 型距离进行比较。聚类数，即不同反应类型的数量，等于队列所占据的可实现趋势模式的数量，并通过重采样加以验证。将该方法应用于 1283 例五点 OGTT，识别出 7 种血糖类型和 8 种胰岛素类型。该数目在三倍的分辨率范围内保持不变。在与六种经典聚类方法的基准比较中，只有我们的方法从不混淆相反的趋势，同时重建误差和稳定性相当。在聚类之后评估的临床正常性是分级的、相互重叠的，并且在各反应类型之间分布不均（$h=0.14$–$0.48$）。总体而言，我们的方法能够区分那些对基于对齐的方法而言过短、但对简化为汇总值而言信息量过大的曲线之间的反应类型。它适用于任何在短网格上记录系统对标准化扰动的反应的方案。

abstract: [Artificial intelligence in medicine] Venous thromboembolism (VTE) continues to pose a substantial health issue worldwide, characterized by high rates of mortality and morbidity. The field of artificial intelligence (AI) has shown potential as a valuable asset for enhancing the detection and prediction of complex diseases, such as VTE. This review explores the role of AI in VTE prediction and diagnosis, analyzing various machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) approaches, including natural language processing (NLP), support vector machines (SVM), random forests (RF), logistic regression (LR), gradient boosting methods, and deep learning frameworks such as ClotCatcher. Among the artificial intelligence models, those based on natural language processing algorithms, particularly ClotCatcher, demonstrated strong performance in analyzing unstructured clinical data. ClotCatcher achieved exceptional Area under the Curve (AUC) values of 0.980 and 0.995 for venous thromboembolism (VTE) adjudication from radiology reports. AI-driven methodologies facilitate early detection, personalized risk assessment, and enhanced patient outcomes. AI holds great potential for improving VTE diagnosis and risk assessment, offering greater accuracy and efficiency than traditional methods. However, further studies are required to validate these models across diverse populations and clinical environments. The integration of AI in VTE management represents a promising frontier in personalized medicine, potentially leading to improved outcomes and more efficient healthcare delivery.

abstract: [Current oncology (Toronto, Ont.)] (1) Background: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains a leading cause of cancer mortality, largely due to late-stage diagnosis and early metastatic progression. Identification of patients with hereditary pancreatic cancer syndromes and familial pancreatic cancer (FPC) provides an opportunity to establish routine surveillance aimed at detecting precursor lesions and early-stage disease. (2) Methods: A narrative review was conducted to evaluate hereditary PDAC susceptibility genes, current screening recommendations, prospective surveillance studies in high-risk individuals, and emerging biomarker, artificial intelligence, risk stratification, and early cancer interception strategies. (3) Results: Germline pathogenic variants, including BRCA1, BRCA2, PALB2, ATM, CDKN2A, STK11, and PRSS1 are associated with increased lifetime PDAC risk. Guidelines recommend surveillance with magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography (MRCP) and endoscopic ultrasound (EUS) for defined high-risk individuals (HRIs). Surveillance programs detect earlier-stage, more frequently resectable disease with encouraging rates of 5-year overall survival. Serum carbohydrate antigen 19-9 (CA 19-9) remains the only current guideline-referenced biomarker, with emerging liquid biopsy, artificial intelligence (AI)/machine learning (ML), and risk-enrichment strategies aimed at improving early-stage detection. (4) Conclusions: Germline testing and high-risk surveillance facilitate earlier PDAC detection and are associated with longer survival in non-randomized studies. Ongoing efforts seek to refine patient selection, resource utilization, surveillance strategies, and biomarker integration to further enhance outcomes.

abstract: [Dentistry journal] Background/Objectives: The cross-sectional classification of mandibular growth-rotation morphology is relevant to orthodontic diagnosis and treatment planning, but conventional structural assessment is observer-dependent. This study developed and internally evaluated deep learning models for classifying existing clockwise and counterclockwise mandibular growth-rotation phenotypes on lateral cephalometric radiographs; it did not forecast future longitudinal growth. Methods: Eight hundred untreated radiographs from individuals aged 9-20 years were labelled by consensus using Björk and Skieller morphological indicators (clockwise, n = 376; counterclockwise, n = 424). A stratified 80:20 training-validation split was used. ResNet50, InceptionV3, and VGG16 were fine-tuned after Gaussian noise reduction, min-max normalisation, and limited geometric augmentation. Results: VGG16 showed the most favourable validation accuracy-loss profile. The archived aggregate confusion matrix (n = 800) yielded an apparent accuracy of 81.13% (95% CI, 78.38-83.75) and balanced accuracy of 81.32% (95% CI, 78.62-83.96); recall was 84.57% for clockwise and 78.07% for counterclockwise phenotypes. Because the matrix included the complete labelled cohort, these values are descriptive apparent performance and not an independent test estimate. Conclusions: VGG16 can classify cross-sectional mandibular growth-rotation phenotypes with promising apparent performance. External, longitudinal, and observer-benchmark validation is required before clinical use.

abstract: [Biosensors] Non-invasive salivary cortisol measurement requires separation of receptor binding from matrix effects and measurement artefacts. We combined a 1550 nanometre dual-graphene optical transducer with an antibody-functionalised cortisol assay and two separately evaluated artificial intelligence workflows. For structural modelling, 8192 scrambled Sobol proposals yielded 7941 accepted geometries. Grouped development selected an extremely randomised tree ensemble, whose sealed-test coefficient of determination was 0.986. Genetic and particle swarm searches were performed after model freeze, and direct transfer-matrix calculations gave a leading candidate sensitivity of 198.60 degrees per refractive-index unit and a resonance width of 0.1790 degrees. These computational candidates were distinct from the nominal cartridge used experimentally. The receptor-functionalised assay had a detection limit of 0.15 nanograms per millilitre and a validated quantitative range of 0.25-8.00 nanograms per millilitre. A gradient-boosted model using complete target and reference angular traces achieved mean absolute errors of 0.25 and 0.50 nanograms per millilitre in 25 blinded artificial-saliva samples and 40 human-saliva samples, respectively; conventional calibration gave corresponding errors of 0.34 and 0.62. Human-saliva measurements were compared with isotope-dilution liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry. Nominal 90% prediction intervals achieved 92% and 90% coverage. The nominal optical advantage over the simpler AZO/graphene reference was incremental, and residual cortisone cross-reactivity remained. These results support a proof-of-concept biosensor requiring further manufacturing and external clinical evaluation.

abstract: [Dentistry journal] Background/Objectives: Artificial intelligence (AI) research in endodontics has grown quickly, but the strength of the evidence differs between applications. This narrative review with structured evidence mapping examined diagnostic imaging, canal morphology, outcome prediction, large language models (LLMs), robotics and augmented reality, and operational uses such as case-difficulty assessment, triage and scheduling. Methods: Two anchor reviews were combined with a documented PubMed search to 30 September 2026, and studies were classified by design, sample, reference standard, validation, and evidence of clinical utility. Results: Periapical lesion detection has the largest evidence base: one meta-analysis reported pooled sensitivity of 0.925 and specificity of 0.852, although most included studies were at risk of bias and none was prospective. Fracture detection relies mainly on ex vivo data and is sensitive to image resolution. Outcome models showed modest to moderate discrimination in single-centre data. LLM studies reported 40% to 100% correct, appropriate, or concordant responses across different benchmarks and scoring rules, and outputs varied on repeated querying. Difficulty-assessment and scheduling tools have appeared since 2020 but have not been evaluated prospectively in clinical workflow.
